test_title: PYST 31: SSC MTS 2024 - General Awareness (Held On: 22 Oct, 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s².
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 2.5 kW**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The escalator raises 20 people per minute to a height of 15 metres. Each person has an average mass of 50 kg.
 
• The gravitational force acting on each person is calculated as **weight = mass × gravity**, which is 50 kg × 10 m/s² = 500 N.
 
• The work done to raise one person is **work = force × height**, which is 500 N × 15 m = 7500 J.
 
• For 20 people, the total work done per minute is 7500 J × 20 = 150,000 J.
 
• Power is calculated as **power = work done / time**. Since time is 60 seconds (1 minute), the power of the escalator is 150,000 J / 60 s = 2500 W or 2.5 kW.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Work:** In physics, work is defined as the product of force applied and displacement in the direction of the force. It is measured in joules (J).
 
• **Power:** Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. The unit of power is watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** The force exerted by gravity on an object is calculated as mass × acceleration due to gravity (g), which is approximately 9.8 m/s² but rounded to 10 m/s² for simplification.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** In machines like escalators, mechanical energy is used to lift objects or people against gravity, converting electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• **Efficiency:** Practical escalators may have less efficiency due to friction and other factors, but theoretical calculations assume ideal conditions.
